Check out our [platform support page](https://pypdfium2-team.github.io/pypdfium2/platforms.html). 17: 18: pypdfium2 includes [helpers](#support-model) to simplify common use cases, while the [raw PDFium API](#raw-pdfium-api) (ctypes) remains accessible as well. 19: 20: 21: ## Installation 22: 23: ### From PyPI (recommended) 24: ```bash 25: python -m pip install -U pypdfium2 26: ``` 27: If available for your platform, this will use a pre-built wheel package, which is the easiest way of installing pypdfium2. 28: Otherwise, [setup code](#from-the-repository--with-setup) will run. 29: If your platform is not covered with pre-built binaries, this will look for system pdfium, or attempt to build pdfium from source. 30: 31: #### JavaScript/XFA builds 32: 33: pdfium-binaries also offer V8 (JavaScript) / XFA enabled builds. 34: If you need them, do e.g.: 35: ```bash 36: PDFIUM_PLATFORM=auto-v8 pip install -v pypdfium2 --no-binary pypdfium2 37: ``` 38: This will bypass wheels and run setup, while requesting use of V8 builds through the `PDFIUM_PLATFORM=auto-v8` environment setting. See below for more info. 39: 40: #### Optional runtime dependencies 41: 42: As of this writing, pypdfium2 does not require any mandatory runtime dependencies, apart from Python and PDFium itself (which is commonly bundled). 43: 44: However, some optional support model / CLI features need additional packages: 45: * [`Pillow`](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) (module `PIL`) is a popular imaging library for Python. 46: pypdfium2 provides convenience adapters to translate between raw bitmap buffers and PIL images. 47: It also uses PIL for some command-line functionality (e.g. image saving). 48: * [`NumPy`](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/index.html) is a library for scientific computing. 49: As with `Pillow`, pypdfium2 provides helpers to get a numpy array view of a raw bitmap. 50: * [`opencv-python`](https://github.com/opencv/opencv-python) (module `cv2`) is an imaging library built around numpy arrays. 51: It can be used in the rendering CLI to save with pypdfium2's numpy adapter. 52: * If [`tabulate`](https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate) is installed, the CLI will give prettier output where tables are involved. 53: 54: pypdfium2 tries to defer imports of optional dependencies until they are actually needed, so there should be no startup overhead if you don't use them. 55: 56: 57: ### From the repository / With setup 58: 59: _Note, unlike helpers, pypdfium2's setup is not bound by API stability promises, so it may change any time._ 60: 61: #### Setup Dependencies 62: 63: *System* 64: + C pre-processor (`gcc`/`clang` – alternatively, specify the command to invoke via `$CPP`) 65: + `git` (Used e.g. to determine the latest pdfium-binaries version, to get `git describe` info, or to check out pdfium on sourcebuild. Might be optional on default setup.) 66: + [`gh >= 2.47.0`](https://github.com/cli/cli/) (optional; used to verify pdfium-binaries build attestations) 67: 68: *Python* 69: + [`ctypesgen` (pypdfium2-team fork)](https://github.com/pypdfium2-team/ctypesgen) 70: + `setuptools` 71: + `wheel`, if setuptools is `< v70.1.0` 72: 73: Python dependencies should be automatically installed, unless `--no-build-isolation` is passed to pip. 74: 75: > [!NOTE] 76: > pypdfium2 and its ctypesgen fork are developed in sync, i.e. each pypdfium2 commit ought to be coupled with the then `HEAD` of pypdfium2-ctypesgen.
77: > Our release sdists, and latest pypdfium2 from git, will automatically use matching ctypesgen.
78: > However, when using a non-latest commit, you'll have to set up the right ctypesgen version on your own, and install pypdfium2 without build isolation. 79: 80: > [!CAUTION] 81: > **ctypesgen works best on Linux.** 82: > Caution is advised when building bindings natively on other OSes.
83: > In particular, there have been some known bindings generation issues on Windows, when system headers are involved. 84: > Consider opting into the [reference bindings](autorelease/bindings.py) via `PDFIUM_BINDINGS=reference`. 85: 86: #### Get the code 87: 88: ```bash 89: git clone "https://github.com/pypdfium2-team/pypdfium2.git" 90: cd pypdfium2/ 91: ``` 92: 93: #### Default setup 94: 95: ```bash 96: # In the pypdfium2/ directory 97: python -m pip install -v . 98: ``` 99: 100: This will invoke pypdfium2's `setup.py`. Typically, this means a binary will be downloaded from `pdfium-binaries` and bundled into pypdfium2, and ctypesgen will be called on pdfium headers to produce the bindings interface. 101: 102: `pdfium-binaries` offer GitHub build provenance [attestations](https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/attestations), so it is highly recommended that you install the `gh` CLI for our setup to verify authenticity of the binaries. 103: 104: If no pre-built binaries are available for your platform, setup will [look for system pdfium](#with-system-pdfium), or attempt to [build pdfium from source](#with-self-built-pdfium). 105: 106: ##### `pip` options of interest 107: 108: - `-v`: Verbose logging output. Useful for debugging. 109: - `-e`: Install in editable mode, so the installation points to the source tree. This way, changes directly take effect without needing to re-install. Recommended for development. 110: - `--no-build-isolation`: Do not isolate setup in a virtual env; use the main env instead. This renders `pyproject.toml [build-system]` inactive, so setup deps must be prepared by caller. Useful to install custom versions of setup deps, or as speedup when installing repeatedly. 111: - `--no-binary pypdfium2`: Do not use binary *wheels* when installing from PyPI – instead, use the sdist and run setup. Note, this option is improperly named, as pypdfium2's setup will attempt to use binaries all the same. If you want to prevent that, set e.g. `PDFIUM_PLATFORM=fallback` to achieve the same behavior as if there were no pdfium-binaries for the host. Or if you just want to package a source distribution, set `PDFIUM_PLATFORM=sdist`. 112: - `--pre` to install a beta release, if available. 113: 114: 115: #### With system pdfium 116: 117: ```bash 118: PDFIUM_PLATFORM="system-search" python -m pip install -v . 119: ``` 120: 121: Look for a system-provided pdfium shared library, and bind against it. 122: 123: Standard, portable [`ctypes.util.find_library()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/ctypes.html#finding-shared-libraries) means will be used to probe for system pdfium at setup time, and the result will be hardcoded into the bindings. Alternatively, set `$PDFIUM_BINARY` to the path of the out-of-tree DLL to use. 124: 125: If system pdfium was found, we will look for pdfium headers from which to generate the bindings (e.g. in `/usr/include`). If the headers are in a location not recognized by our code, set `$PDFIUM_HEADERS` to the directory in question. 126: 127: Also, we try to determine the pdfium version, either from the library filename itself, or via `pkg-config`. 128: If this fails, you can pass the version alongside the setup target, e.g. `PDFIUM_PLATFORM=system-search:XXXX`, where `XXXX` is the pdfium build version. 129: If the version is not known in the end, `NaN` placeholders will be set. 130: 131: If the version is known but no headers were found, they will be downloaded from upstream. 132: If neither headers nor version are known (or ctypesgen is not installed), the reference bindings will be used as a last resort.
